summary: 3 of 4 findings resolved. F1 partially wired on frontend; API does not yet produce IncompatibleGroupError.

findings.description: CompatibilityGuard now receives structured IncompatibleGroupError from controller (not always null)
evidence: extractIncompatibleGroupError uses Value.Check(IncompatibleGroupError, error.response) to parse API response (line 33-38)
CompatibilityGuard receives incompatibleGroupError instead of hardcoded null in PowderizerPage.tsx (line 137)
Both quote-fail and mutation-fail call extractIncompatibleGroupError
findings.defect: API error handler at apps/api/src/app.ts:233-235 returns { code, error, field } when PowderMixDomainError is thrown. The validateMixingGroupCompat function in powderMixRules.ts throws MIX_COMPONENT_INELIGIBLE � not MIXING_GROUP_MISMATCH � and provides no conflictingProductIds or groupInfo. Value.Check(IncompatibleGroupError, error.response) will always return null because the API response shape never matches the IncompatibleGroupError schema.
findings.recommendation: Either: (a) update validateMixingGroupCompat in powderMixRules.ts to produce a structured IncompatibleGroupError response, or (b) add a controller-level fallback that synthesizes IncompatibleGroupError from PowderMixDomainError fields when code is MIX_COMPONENT_INELIGIBLE and products have conflicting mixingGroup. Current wiring is correct frontend architecture but non-functional end-to-end.

findings.description: New tests for CompatibilityGuard and IngredientPicker
evidence: CompatibilityGuard.test.tsx: 5 tests � null render, mismatch display with names/groups, unknown name fallback (Product ID), null mixingGroup fallback (Group: unknown), 3+ conflicting products
IngredientPicker.test.tsx: 6 tests � incompatible disable, incompatible marking, null mixingGroup no-restrict, max-5-disables-add, category filter + pagination (10->4 results), empty state
All 40 tests pass across 9 test files in powderizer + customPowder suites
No test assertions against mock � all tests exercise real components with controlled product data

notes: F1 frontend architecture is correct and safely degrades (null passes through to CompatibilityGuard which renders nothing). The fix fulfills its stated scope: frontend is wired, contracts define the schema, tests cover rendering. However, the end-to-end mixing-group error UX is non-functional until the API produces the structured IncompatibleGroupError. Recommend filing a follow-up for API-side work and then adding an integration test that asserts the full round-trip.
